- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+), leading to overshoot; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 85→70, 80→70), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 2–3 periods after peak.  
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true trend by 1–2 periods; if sentiment is trending, shift forecast 1–2 periods ahead to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.33, +1.00, -0.33), model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
